== Overview & Architectural Fit ==
'''Dedalus''' solves partial differential equations by spectral methods. Equations and boundary conditions are entered symbolically, close to how they are written on paper; the solution is expanded as <math>u(x,t) = \sum_n \hat{u}_n(t)\,\phi_n(x)</math> on Cartesian domains, disks, annuli, spheres and shells, in parallel with MPI. It solves initial-value, boundary-value and eigenvalue problems.

== Mathematical Evaluation for TPM ==
* '''Lagrangian / Action (2/10):''' Takes equations, not actions.
* '''Field / PDE (9/10):''' Spectrally accurate, with flexible entry of equations.
* '''Relativity (2/10):''' Not a relativity code; at most linear equations on a fixed background.
* '''Quantum / Data (3/10):''' Can integrate Schr&ouml;dinger or Gross-Pitaevskii equations; nothing learns from data.

== Integration Pipeline ==
# '''Take the Euler-Lagrange field equations''' derived with [[The Principia Machina/Tools/SymPy|SymPy]] or [[The Principia Machina/Tools/xAct|xAct]].
# '''Solve''' them as an initial-value problem.
# '''Monitor the Noether charges''' (energy, momentum, angular momentum): at spectral accuracy, any drift beyond the time-stepping error is a sharp sign of a fault in the derivation or the discretization.
# '''Solve the eigenvalue problem''' <math>\lambda M x = L x</math> of the second variation, for the linear stability of an extremum of the action.

== Status, Licence and Limits ==
* '''Status:''' Active. Version 3.0.5, 31 January 2026 (PyPI).
* '''Licence:''' GPL-3.0.
* '''Home:''' https://dedalus-project.org
* '''Limits:''' Domains are limited to geometries a spectral basis can represent. Shocks and non-smooth solutions fit poorly. The GPL may matter for redistribution.

== On the Principia Machina ==
A tool runs only where the sponsor installed and bound it, and what it returns is untrusted input, vetted before use; its numbers are never values of the site's calculator, TPC. A value it computes lands as a RESULT with QUANTITY, VALUE, UNIT and AT, its initial and boundary values as SITUATION records; the regime of a numerical result, and whether such a value may be presented, are open questions of the specification. See [[The Principia Machina/Agent/Tools|Agent/Tools]] and [[The Principia Machina/Tools/Operator's guide|the operator's guide]].
